text:
<u>The **Fleet Sharing submodule** allows users to create, manage, and monitor fleet sharing records.</u>

* <u>Click on **+ New fleet sharing** for creating new record</u>

* <u>Click **Filters** to access filtering options.</u>

* <u>Search for the required Fleet sharing by selecting the desired **Period** or by entering the subject in</u> <u>the **Search by tittle.**</u>

* <u>Click **Apply** to filter the records or **Clear** to reset the filters.</u>

* <u>Use the action icons to manage the selected Fleet sharing (See Figure 2).</u>

breadcrumb: Audit - Fleet Sharing Manual- Office_R1_30.06.2026 > 3.2 ACTIONS (p.6)
text:
<u>This section allows users to create and manage actions that are required to be completed by the vessels.</u>

* Click **+ Add Action** to create a new action. (See Figure 4)

  * In the **Add Action window**, enter the mandatory details marked with (**\***), including the Nature of Action and Due Date. (See figure 5)

  * Click **Save** to add the action to the Fleet Sharing record.

  * Repeat the above steps to add additional actions, if required.

* Click the **Edit** icon to modify an existing action.

* Click the **Delete** icon to remove an action.

* Click **Upload** to attach supporting documents related to the action.

* Click **View** to open or delete the uploaded attachments.
  (See Figure 4,5).

text:
Each question in the Preparation Checklist is supplemented with additional guidance and reference information based on the SIRE 2.0 Question Library.

These details assist users in understanding the inspection requirements and include Industry and Company guidance, expected evidence, grounds for negative observations, classification, assigned risk level, repeated observations, and verification responsibilities.

breadcrumb: Audit - Preparation Manual_Office_R1_30.06.2026 > 6.2 SEMI ONLINE MODE (p.32)
text:
Semi-Online mode allows users to continue working without an active internet connection and synchronize their changes once connectivity is restored.

* <u>All data entered while in Semi-Online mode is stored in the device's local database.</u>

* <u>Once an internet connection is available, the locally stored data can be synchronized with</u> <u>the cloud server.</u>

breadcrumb: Audit - Preparation Manual_Office_R1_30.06.2026 > 6.1 ONLINE MODE (p.31)
text:
When the application is connected to the internet, it operates in **Online** mode. (See Figure 45).

* <u>All data is automatically synchronized with the cloud server in real time whenever you save</u> <u>your work.</u>

* <u>Click **Save** to save the latest changes. A confirmation message is displayed once the data is</u> <u>successfully saved. (See Figure 46)</u>

* <u>During the save process, the **Online** status changes to **Saving** (orange). Once synchronization</u> <u>is complete, the status changes back to **Online** (green).</u>

* <u>Clicking **Next** or **Back** also saves the current data before navigating to the next or previous</u> <u>chapter.</u>

[!NOTE]
While the **Saving** (orange) status is displayed, the data is first stored in the device's local database before being synchronized to the cloud. This prevents data loss in the event of an internet interruption or if the user subsequently switches to **Semi-Online** mode.

<u>If the internet connection is lost while working in Online mode:</u>

These tasks define the daily work and rest hour patterns for crew members. (Ref Figure 98) * Each crew member is displayed in two separate rows: * Sea Routine – Applicable while at sea. * Port Routine – Applicable while in port. * **Variable Tasks**: Variable Tasks are one-time events or operations involving multiple crew members that occur outside the standard daily routine, such as drills, bunkering, and port calls. breadcrumb: Safety - MOC User Manual_Office_R0_31.03.2026 > 2. MoC DASHBOARD (p.5)
text:
<u>Introduction:</u>

The **MOC Dashboard** provides a centralized overview of all **Management of Change (MOC)** records.

It enables users to monitor the progress of ongoing MOCs, track pending actions and overdue changes, and review KPIs through **Operational** and **Management** dashboard views.

* Upon entering the **MOC** sub-module, the **Dashboard** is displayed by default.

* The Dashboard provides two views: **Operational** and **Management**.

* Select **Operational** or **Management** to switch between the respective dashboard views. *(See Figure 3)*

breadcrumb: Safety - MOC User Manual_Office_R0_31.03.2026 > 2.2 Management Dashboard (p.6)
text:
The **Management Dashboard** provides a graphical overview of MOC performance through **Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)**, **periodic analysis**, and **change analysis**. It enables users to monitor MOC performance and review change trends across vessels.

* **Status Summary** displays the total number of **In Progress**, **Extended**, and **Overdue** MOC records.

* **KPI MoC** displays key performance indicators related to MOC processing, completion, effectiveness, and approval status.

* **Periodic Analysis** displays graphical trends of MOC records and associated risk levels over a selected period.

* **Change Analysis** displays graphical summaries of changes based on parameters such as **Nature of Change**, **Reason for Change**, and **Type of Change**

(See Figure 4)

text:
The Operational Dashboard provides a centralized overview of ongoing MOC’s enabling users to monitor approved MOCs in progress, overdue MOCs, extensions, and pending actions.

* **Approved MOCs in Progress** – Displays approved MOCs currently under implementation.

* **MOCs Overdue** – Displays MOCs that have exceeded their target completion date.

* **MOCs with Extension** – Displays MOCs for which the completion date has been extended.

* **Pending Actions** – Displays outstanding actions along with their due dates and responsible personnel.

▪ Click the **Edit icon** beside the respective entry to open and view the corresponding **MoC record**. *(See Figure 3)*

breadcrumb: Safety - SMS User Manual_Office_R0_31.01.2026 > 3.2 DASHBOARD (p.12)
text:
* SMS change request forms can be viewed from the Dashboard.

* Dashboard is divided into two sections: *New Document* and *New Revision*.

  * **New Document** – Displays the record of change requests for documents uploaded in SAIL for the first time.

  * **New Revision** – Displays the record of change requests for revisions uploaded to existing documents.

* Each section includes the following stages:

  * **Draft** – Contains change request forms that are in the proposal stage and have not yet been submitted for approval.

  * **Pending for Approval** – Displays forms that have been submitted for approval but are not yet approved.

  * **Approved** – Displays forms that have been approved by the approver but are not yet released.

  * **Rejected** – Displays forms that have been rejected by the approver.

  * **Released** – The final stage; displays forms that have been released for vessel and office use.

* Upon entering the ‘Ship’s Certificates’ sub-submodule, the system automatically opens the ‘Master’ tab by default, allowing users to view all certificate details:

  * **Master Tab**: The Master tab serves as the central repository for all certificate master records available in the system. It allows administrators to define and maintain certificate types, categories, groups, regulatory references, and certificate labels. This view establishes the standard certificate structure that can be applied across companies and vessels. (Ref Figure 12)

  * **Company Tab**: The Company tab displays certificate records configured for individual companies. It allows administrators to review company-specific certificate requirements, certificate labels, regulatory references, and company group assignments. This view helps ensure that the appropriate certificate masters are assigned and maintained at the company level. (Ref Figure 12)

  * **Vessel Tab**: The Vessel tab displays certificate records applicable

text: * Running Hours (RH) tracks the total operating hours of machinery components. Many PMS jobs are triggered by running hours rather than calendar dates — for example, 'overhaul every 4,000 hours'. Accurate RH updates are essential for the maintenance schedule to function correctly.

* Hand icon **Scheduled**: Jobs that have been planned and have a future due date.
* **Due**: Jobs that are due within the current period.
* **Overdue**: Jobs past their due date that have not been completed.
* **Postponed**: Jobs that have been deferred with an approved justification.
* **Unplanned**: Details of unplanned work orders will be displayed in this section.
* **Pending Approval**: All submitted work order details will be displayed here for HOD approval.
* **Completed**: Fully executed and approved ‘Work Order’ details will be displayed in this tab.
